gp.heading: Gross Profit
gp.text:
Gross profit represents net revenue less cost of revenue. Cost of revenue consists primarily of the cost of raw material components, subcontract labor assembly from contract manufacturers, direct and indirect personnel expenses related to professional services, manufacturing overhead, inventory reserves for excess and obsolete products or raw materials, warranty costs, royalties and share-based compensation.

The following table presents our gross profit:

Gross profit as a percentage of revenue (referred to as “gross margin”) remained consistent for both periods in the table above. Our revenue mix in the current quarter was more heavily weighted toward certain lower-margin embedded compute products compared to the prior year period. The impact on our gross margin in the current quarter was positively offset by additional SaaS revenue from Nero, along with lower inventory charges and overhead costs compared to the prior year.

We currently expect that gross margin will fluctuate in future periods based on, among other factors, changes in our product mix, average selling prices, and average manufacturing costs.

rd.heading: Research and Development
rd.text:
Research and development expenses consist of personnel-related expenses, share-based compensation, and expenditures to third-party vendors for research and development activities and product certification costs. Our quarterly costs related to outside services and product certifications vary from period to period depending on our level and timing of development activities.

The following table presents our research and development expenses:

Research and development expenses decreased primarily due to (i) lower spending on outside services, including outsourced product development and contractor costs, and (ii) lower personnel-related expenses in our engineering team resulting from restructuring activities during the prior fiscal year.

ga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative
ga.text:
Selling, general and administrative expenses consist of personnel-related expenses, including salaries and commissions, share-based compensation, facility expenses, information technology, advertising and marketing expenses, and professional, legal and accounting fees.

The following table presents our selling, general and administrative expenses:

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased primarily due to (i) higher personnel-related expenses related to increased headcount, including employees added from the Nero acquisition, and (ii) higher advertising and marketing costs related to certain promotional and trade show spending.

sga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative
sga.text:
Selling, general and administrative expenses consist of personnel-related expenses, including salaries and commissions, share-based compensation, facility expenses, information technology, advertising and marketing expenses, and professional, legal and accounting fees.

The following table presents our selling, general and administrative expenses:

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased primarily due to (i) higher personnel-related expenses related to increased headcount, including employees added from the Nero acquisition, and (ii) higher advertising and marketing costs related to certain promotional and trade show spending.

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense), Net
nonop.text: Our other income (expense), net, is comprised primarily of foreign currency remeasurement and transaction adjustments related to our foreign subsidiaries whose functional currency is the U.S. dollar.

tax.heading: Provision for Income Taxes
tax.text: Refer to Note 9 of Notes to Unaudited Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, included in Part I, Item 1 of this Report, which is incorporated herein by reference, for a discussion regarding our provision for income taxes.

net.text: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, our net loss included $2,336,000 of non-cash charges, while the changes in operating assets and liabilities used net cash of $4,378,000. We used cash in operating activities during the current quarter primarily as a result of an increase in our inventory balances and the payment of variable accrued compensation, along with the timing of our collections on accounts receivable, payments of accounts payable.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text:
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, our net loss included $2,336,000 of non-cash charges, while the changes in operating assets and liabilities used net cash of $4,378,000. We used cash in operating activities during the current quarter primarily as a result of an increase in our inventory balances and the payment of variable accrued compensation, along with the timing of our collections on accounts receivable, payments of accounts payable.

Accounts receivable increased by $3,577,000, or 14.1%, from June 30, 2026 to September 30, 2026. The increase was primarily due to the higher volume of shipments in the current quarter, as well as the timing of payments from certain customers near quarter-end.

Inventories increased by $5,357,000, or 20.8% from June 30, 2026 to September 30, 2026.

sbc.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses consist of personnel-related expenses, including salaries and commissions, share-based compensation, facility expenses, information technology, advertising and marketing expenses, and professional, legal and accounting fees.

wc.text: On July 7, 2026, we entered into an asset purchase agreement to acquire the industrial IoT business of Vecima, including its Nero platform, for aggregate consideration of approximately $11.6 million, excluding working capital adjustments and other customary purchase price adjustments. The acquired business provides GPS-based fleet and asset tracking solutions and serves customers across the fleet, municipal, restoration and industrial asset-tracking markets in North America. We closed the transaction on August 1, 2026.

capex.text: Net cash used in investing activities for the three months ended September 30, 2026 includes (i) $10,343,000 for the Nero acquisition, (ii) the purchase of marketable securities of $13,800,000, and (iii) purchases of property and equipment totaling $110,000, primarily consisting of computer software.

net sales.heading: Net Revenue
net sales.text: The following tables present our net revenue by product line and by geographic region:

Embedded IoT Solutions.heading: Embedded IoT Solutions
Embedded IoT Solutions.text: Our embedded product portfolio includes a broad range of compute system-on-module (“SoM”) and System-in-Package (“SiP”) solutions, together with wired and wireless connectivity products. As semiconductor technology continues to evolve and integrate more functionality, our compute modules now provide not only processing power but also the ability to run advanced AI and machine learning applications. This enables our customers to process and analyze digital inputs such as video, audio, and sensor data, directly at the device level, reducing latency, enhancing security, and enabling real-time decision making.

IoT System Solutions.heading: IoT System Solutions
IoT System Solutions.text: Our IoT System Solutions portfolio includes a wide range of fully functional standalone systems that provide routing, switching or gateway functionalities as well as telematics and media conversion. These products include wired and wireless connections that enhance the value and utility of modern electronic systems and equipment by providing secure network connectivity, power for IoT end devices through Power over Ethernet (“PoE”), application hosting, protocol conversion, media conversion, secure access for distributed IoT deployments and many other functions. By offering pre-certified products across multiple regions, Lantronix significantly reduces Original Equipment Manufacturer (“OEM”) customers’ regulatory certification costs and speeds up their time-to-market.

Software and Services.heading: Software and Services
Software and Services.text:
Our Software and Services offerings are central to our strategy of increasing recurring, higher margin revenue across each of our vertical markets. Our Percepxion™ Software as a Service (“SaaS”) platform offers comprehensive single-pane-of-glass management for our Out-Of-Band (“OOB”) and Industrial IoT deployments, enabling customers to easily deploy, monitor, manage and automate across their global deployments, all from a single platform login, virtually and seamlessly connected as if located directly on each device. Our platform eliminates the need for 24/7 personnel on site and makes it easy to observe and address issues quickly, even in large-scale deployments. Following our August 2026 acquisition of Nero, our Software and Services portfolio also includes GPS-based vehicle and asset tracking capabilities for fleet, municipal, and industrial asset tracking customers, further broadening our recurring revenue base.

We leverage our deep engineering expertise and product development best practices to deliver high-quality, innovative products cost-effectively and on schedule across each of our three vertical markets.

intro.text: Lantronix Inc. (NASDAQ: LTRX) is a global leader in Edge AI and Industrial IoT solutions that power NDAA-compliant unmanned systems, critical infrastructure and resilient enterprise networks. It delivers intelligent computing, secure connectivity and remote management for mission-critical applications enabling customers to optimize operations, enhance security and accelerate digital transformation. Its comprehensive portfolio of hardware, software and services powers applications ranging from mission-critical autonomous platforms and edge analytics for critical infrastructure to intelligent surveillance and secure network management. By bringing intelligence to the network edge, Lantronix helps organizations achieve efficiency, security and a competitive edge in today’s AI-driven world. For more information, visit the Lantronix website.

lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

Customer C | – * | 13 %
OEMs design and sell products under their own brand that are either manufactured by the OEM in-house or by third-party contract manufacturers.

We depend upon a relatively small number of distributors and end-user customers for a large portion of our revenue, and a decline in sales to these major customers would materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
Our customer concentration could fluctuate, depending on future customer requirements, which will depend on market conditions in the industry segments in which our customers participate.
Some of our integrated circuits are only available from a single source and in some cases, are no longer being manufactured.
Future operating results depend upon our ability to timely obtain components in sufficient quantities and on acceptable terms.
Our ability to sustain and grow our business depends on our ability to develop, market, scale, and sell new products.
As a result, our future prospects will depend on our ability to develop and successfully market new products that address new and growing markets.
We depend on distributors for a majority of our sales and to complete order fulfillment.
We depend on the resale of products through distributor accounts for a substantial majority of our worldwide net revenue.
The duration and extent of a future pandemic’s effect on our operations and financial condition will depend on future developments, which are highly uncertain and cannot be predicted at this time.

We therefore believe that quarter to quarter comparisons of our operating results are not a good indication of our future performance, and investors should not rely on them to predict our future operating or financial performance or the future performance of the market price of our common stock.

Any future decision to declare or pay dividends will be made by the Board in its sole discretion and will depend upon our financial condition, operating results, capital requirements and other factors that the Board deems appropriate at the time of its decision.

Our principal sources of cash and liquidity include our existing cash and cash equivalents, borrowings and amounts available under our existing bank borrowing agreement, and cash generated from operations.
All of our products are manufactured by third-party contract manufacturers and foundries primarily located in Thailand and Taiwan.
